$comment: P65 — `extern` ON A FILE-SCOPE INITIALIZER-INFERRED DECLARATION: the SPECIFIER-SET half of [[D-CSUBSET-AUTO-FILE-SCOPE]] (C23 6.7.2p2). ✔MEASURED before the change through the shipped DSS CLI, `extern auto g = 1;` was error[P_NoAlternativeMatched] and `auto extern g = 1;` was refused IDENTICALLY — which is what makes this a specifier-SET gap and not an ORDER one, since the file-scope specifier run was ALREADY order-free when both spellings failed. ✔THE REFERENCES, each probed SEPARATELY on its own translation unit, 2026-09-08: gcc 13.3.0 `-std=c2x -c` rc=0 with `nm` reading `D g` (DEFINED, EXTERNAL) and a warning "'g' initialized and declared 'extern'", `-pedantic-errors` rc=0; clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23 -c` rc=0 with `nm` `D g` and a -Wextern-initializer warning, `-pedantic-errors` rc=0; MSVC 19.51.36252 ABSTAINS — it implements no C23 inference at all (`auto g = 1;` is rc=0 with warning C4042 "'g': has bad storage class", the C89 STORAGE CLASS over an implicit int, and it refuses `static auto g = 1;` with C2159 too), so its C2159 on `extern auto` is a collision between two storage classes rather than a verdict on this feature; ISO C23 6.7.2p2 lists `auto` as combinable with every storage-class specifier except `typedef` and 6.7.2p4 conditions that on "if the type is to be inferred from an initializer", which is exactly this row. Two working references and ISO C on the accepting side, both -pedantic-errors clean, so DSS was BELOW the union. ★★★ WHAT IT MEANS IS C23 6.7.2p15 — "If auto appears with another storage-class specifier, or if it appears in a declaration at file scope, it is IGNORED for the purposes of determining a storage duration or linkage. In this case, it indicates only that the declared type may be inferred." — so `extern` decides the linkage alone and C 6.9.3p1's file-scope-initializer rule (landed this cycle as [[D-C-FILE-SCOPE-EXTERN-WITH-INITIALIZER-IS-A-DEFINITION]]) makes the declaration a DEFINITION, the `extern` redundant rather than contradictory. THAT IS WHY NO ENGINE LINE MOVED: the fix is two localized edits to c.lang.json — `ExternKeyword` joins `topLevelAutoSpecifier`'s alt, and `autoInferredTopLevelDecl`'s `linkageSpecifiers` gains the SAME `{nonDefining, exclusiveGroup, compatibleWith}` cell `topLevelDecl` already carries for the same keyword. ★★★ THE EXAMPLE IS NOT A PARSE TEST, AND A PARSE-ONLY FIX IS WHAT IT EXISTS TO CATCH: admitting the token in the GRAMMAR alone would have made every declaration rc 0 while the linkage tier answered warning[H_UnknownLinkageSpecifier] and DROPPED the keyword — an accept with the specifier discarded, the exact shape this row's own `register` history records being refuted by measurement. So every arm gates on a RUNTIME consequence: def.c's `extern auto g_ext = 11;` is read here through a plain `extern int g_ext;`, so a mis-lowering to an IMPORT fails the LINK with an undefined symbol while a mis-lowering of the reader into a definition fails it with a DUPLICATE (one arm, both directions); `extern auto e_int = 20;` must define storage here and hold its value; `auto extern r_int = 7;` is the REVERSED order of the same set and must mean the same thing (C 6.7p2); `extern const auto k_dbl = 2.0;` must infer DOUBLE — `k_dbl + k_dbl` truncates to 4, which an int-defaulted type gets wrong — while the leading `const` still binds through a prefix that now also carries `extern`; and `extern auto p_str = "ok";` must DECAY to a pointer (C23 6.7.10p2 infers the type after array-to-pointer conversion) and be indexable. exit = 11 + 20 + 7 + 4 + 0 = 42, and ✔the same two files build and run to 42 under gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3, so the expected value is a reference measurement rather than a DSS self-report. RED-ON-DISABLE (REMOVE direction), TWO INDEPENDENT MUTANTS because the change has two halves and either alone would leave the other unproven. ⚠ BOTH MUTANTS ARE THE CONFIG DOCUMENT, SO NO OBJECT md5 IS INVOLVED: c.lang.json is copied into the build tree's `dss-config-snapshot` at ctest RUN time and never at build time (cmake/DssConfigSnapshot.cmake), so no translation unit recompiles and no binary moves; what moves is the config file's own md5, which must move and RETURN. (A) GRAMMAR — delete "ExternKeyword" from `topLevelAutoSpecifier`'s `alt` in src/dss-config/sources/c.lang.json: every declaration in main.c and def.c becomes error[P_NoAlternativeMatched] and this example never links. (B) SEMANTICS — delete the "extern" entry from `autoInferredTopLevelDecl`'s `linkageSpecifiers`: the declarations still PARSE, which is the point, so the definedness arms fail while a parse-shaped pin would stay green. Both red sets and the green controls are named in tests/analysis/semantic/test_specifier_set_extern_auto_and_inline_object.cpp.

Declared `positioned:false` because the runner resolves a span offset through ONE SourceBuffer and this manifest has two sources; the code is emitted five times (four declarations in main.c, one in def.c) and the set comparison collapses them. ⓘ The warning itself is correct and matches the references: gcc 13.3.0 warns "'g' initialized and declared 'extern'" and clang 18.1.3 warns -Wextern-initializer on exactly this construct.
